title: Obex delegates its executive function to a separate Executor Agent through a re-Invocable Accord
content:
Obex's Executor Accord Primitive is `Active` (A.6.1.1.5.2.2.1.1.1) with one Active Instance: the **Ozone Instance** (A.6.1.1.5.2.2.1.2.1). Its single substantive parameter is a pointer: "The Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps for Ozone are specified in A.6.1.2.2 - Operational Executor Agent Ozone" (A.6.1.1.5.2.2.1.2.1.1.1).

Obex therefore does not staff its own executive function. The roles that actually execute and review — Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps — belong to a separate Executor Agent, and their definitions live in that Agent's Artifact. Obex's document records only that the relationship exists and where to read its terms.

Crucially, this Primitive keeps the standard re-Invocable lifecycle (A.6.1.1.5.2.2.1.1.4), unlike the one-shot Genesis Primitives. An Agent's identity is fixed at genesis, but its executor is not: new Executor Accord Instances can be Invoked, and existing ones can be Completed or Suspended. Who executes for an Agent is designed to be replaceable.

The pattern also creates shared executive capacity. One Executor Agent can hold Accords with several Prime Agents, which means the operational overhead Obex would otherwise duplicate is pooled — the same amortisation logic Obex itself applies to Agent founders, applied one level up to Obex's own operations.

The cost is another traversal: an auditor asking who reviews Obex's Invocations must leave Obex's Artifact entirely to find out.
description: The Ozone Instance of the Executor Accord Primitive is `Active`, and Ozone's Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps are defined in Ozone's own Artifact rather than in Obex's.
